newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Blue chip losses depress Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip losses depress Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Big price losses by blue chips hit trading on the Nigerian stock market on Friday, dealers said.
The all-share index, however, closed barely changed at 6699.36 from 6699.37 on Thursday.
Lever Brothers lost 20 kobo to end the week at 23.60 naira while Cadbury fell 60 kobo to 24.90 naira.
"It is a seasonal thing which takes place around Christmas when people sell shares to raise money," one trader said.
ADC Airlines fell 15 kobo to 4.15 naira, its second day of sliding over the grounding of its operations by the government following the crash of its Boeing 727 plane two weeks ago.
Traders said the future of the stock was uncertain as there could be a run on the shares in the coming week unless the exchange placed it on technical suspension.
Lack of buyers was responsible for Dunlop's fall to 10.50 naira and Guaranty Trust Bank to 13.20 naira. Both lost 20 kobo each.
But positive movements were recorded by oil, cement and most food shares.
Nestle went 50 kobo up to 43.50 naira, Union Dicon Salt added 40 kobo to touch 40.50 naira and National Salt Company gained five at 5.95 naira.
National Oil finished 40 kobo up at 41.50 naira, Agip was 38 kobo more at 18.00 naira and Unipetrol, at 51.00 naira, rose by 20 kobo.

There was renewed interest in Benue Cement Company which jumped 18 kobo to 8.05 naira and the Cement Company of Northern Nigeria which closed four kobo up at 3.00 naira. Sectoral leader West African Portland Cement climbed 20 kobo to 39.20 naira.
AIICO Insurance added 15 kobo to 9.10 naira on positive perception.
